claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and adequately supported because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and any segment-specific gap can be handled through model-card documentation and post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: A material weakness affecting a contractual customer segment or named launch use case must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate launch readiness and rehearsal results can support operational readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy a separate disclosure or approval requirement.
Public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring is supportive context, not a substitute for satisfying the internal policy predicate.
Admissible support must show either resolution of the material gap, approved risk acceptance, or confirmed required disclosure.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual approval or risk-acceptance record authorizing launch despite the telehealth segment gap.
Provide the final disclosure decision from legal/compliance, including whether the limitation must be disclosed pre-launch.
Provide the exact customer commitments showing the affected telehealth discharge planning segment is named, and how launch artifacts map to those commitments.
Provide the final model card or launch documentation showing the limitation disclosure language, if already prepared.
Provide the source record for the segment-level target, observed miss, and any remediation or waiver status.
specific_concerns: The actor's own summary says the telehealth discharge planning segment misses target and is named in customer commitments, which fits the stated policy definition of materiality.
Legal review is still open, and the policy text says product labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending.
The packet appears to rely on aggregate readiness and monitoring, but policy compliance turns on the unresolved materiality/disclosure predicate for a named launch use case or contractual segment.
No admissible evidence in the summary shows the limitation has been resolved before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance.
No admissible evidence in the summary confirms the required disclosure will in fact be included in launch materials or the model card.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record without a resolved disclosure determination or approved risk acceptance.
That aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are sufficient to overcome a material segment-specific gap for a named committed use case.
That post-launch monitoring alone satisfies the policy requirement tied to material limitations.
